name: io.shipfolio/shipfolio
title: Shipfolio
description: Verified indie SaaS revenue, tech stacks and alternatives. Check any product by its website.

tools.name: list_niches
tools.description: The curated niche list: the only niches update_my_listing, create_article_draft and update_article_draft accept. Search by name or synonym ("fintech" finds Finance); without a query, every niche A to Z, 50 at most. Pass the slug to write tools. A niche that isn't on the list can only be proposed by the person, in the editor.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "time tracking"; leave out for the whole list

tools.name: search_articles
tools.description: Articles and guides founders wrote about building, launching and growing their products. Filter by words in the title, a niche or the product; latest first or most read. At most 20 a page, 5 pages; each links to the article. Call get_article to read one.

query.description: Words in the title or excerpt

product.description: A product's slug, for articles about it

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: One published article in full: its Markdown body, author, the product it is about, how many people liked it, and its comments (the first 20, each reply right after the comment it answers, the author's own marked). Lines like ::embed{id="…"} are charts and cards the page draws; cite the url for them. Liking and commenting happen on shipfolio.io, not here.

slug.description: The article's slug, the last part of shipfolio.io/articles/{slug} (search_articles finds it)

tools.name: get_founder
tools.description: A person's public Shipfolio profile: headline, bio, their products, work history and recent ship log. Contact details are never included; to reach someone, link them to their profile.

tools.name: get_company
tools.description: A company's public page: about, website, its public products and, when the company shows it, its team.

slug.description: The company's slug, as in shipfolio.io/companies/{slug}

tools.name: get_product_timeline
tools.description: A product's build-in-public history and traction over time ("how has X grown", "what has X shipped"): its verified timeline, newest first, 20 events a page: releases from its changelog, verified MRR milestones and month-over-month changes, stack changes (a migration reads "Switched from X to Y" with the founder's reason), launches, articles, infrastructure cost when the founder shares it, and weekly updates. Each event says who verified it (Stripe, RevenueCat, AppStore, GooglePlay, GitHub, Shipfolio or Founder): say so when citing a figure. Money is in cents. Traffic is never on it.

slug.description: The product's slug, e.g. "trackwise" (search_products finds it)

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Find indie SaaS, micro-SaaS and apps by what they do, niche, pricing or a tool in their stack, with revenue verified from Stripe, RevenueCat, App Store Connect or Google Play (never self-reported). Use for "tools for invoicing", "products in developer-tools", "micro-SaaS making over $1K MRR", "apps built with Supabase". An MRR range (minMrrUsd/maxMrrUsd) matches the verified MRR each product shows publicly. Pages hold at most 20 results and stop at page 5, so narrow the filters instead of paging. Each result links to its page on shipfolio.io; call get_product for the full page, or verify_product to check a product by its website.

query.description: Words in the product's name or tagline, e.g. "invoice"

niche.description: A niche tag in lower-kebab case, e.g. "developer-tools" (niche_overview lists related ones)

tool.description: A tool slug the product's stack must include, e.g. "supabase" or "stripe" (search_tools finds slugs)

pricing.description: How the product charges: Free, Freemium, Subscription, OneTime, UsageBased or OpenSource

verifiedRevenueOnly.description: Only products with revenue verified from Stripe, RevenueCat, App Store Connect or Google Play

minMrrUsd.description: Minimum verified MRR in whole US dollars

maxMrrUsd.description: Maximum verified MRR in whole US dollars

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Everything Shipfolio shows about one product: what it does, who makes it, pricing, niches, its stack, launch, recent ship log, verified MRR exactly as the page shows it (and which provider verified it), features, FAQs, the products it is an alternative to, similar products, the product's own social accounts, and its rating with up to 5 reviews (featured ones first, then the newest). When the founder shares both, margin is last full month's verified MRR against its cloud bill (rounded, with the providers), so absent means not shared, never zero. For its full history call get_product_timeline; for its stack in detail, get_product_stack. Each distinct product you open counts toward a daily limit, so open the ones the user cares about rather than every search result.

slug.description: The product's slug, the last part of shipfolio.io/p/{slug}

tools.name: verify_product
tools.description: Check whether a product is real and what is verified about it, by its website (best) or its name: "is X legit", "how much does X make", "who is behind X". Answers a verdict to quote, whether its team claimed its Shipfolio page, its MRR as verified by Stripe, RevenueCat, App Store Connect or Google Play, and its full page. When Shipfolio has no page for the website it says so and queues the product so a page appears (unverified until its team claims it). Counts as opening the product, like get_product.

name.description: The product's name, when the website isn't known, e.g. "Trackwise"

tools.name: get_product_stack
tools.description: What a product is built with ("what tech stack does X use"): every tool in its stack by category, the founder's notes and monthly costs where shared, and the stack analysis (summary, failure points, optimizations) when there is one.

tools.name: compare_stacks
tools.description: Compare two products' tech stacks side by side: the tools they share and the ones only each uses, with a link to the comparison page.

tools.name: product_alternatives
tools.description: Alternatives and competitors to a named product, e.g. "alternatives to Notion" or "Linear competitors": indie products whose makers list them as an alternative to it, each with its verified revenue when it has some. The named product doesn't have to be on Shipfolio. Up to 20, with a link to the full alternatives page.

product.description: The product's slug or name, e.g. "notion"

tools.name: niche_overview
tools.description: A market niche at a glance ("what's in the AI writing space"): how many public products are in it, the top 10, the tools they use most and related niches. Use search_products with the niche to go further.

tools.name: launches
tools.description: New product launches ("what launched today", "this week's new SaaS"): Shipfolio's launch board, products launching on a UTC day ranked by upvotes, or the week or month ending on that day. Defaults to today. At most 50.

day.description: The UTC day, yyyy-MM-dd; today when left out

tools.name: making_money
tools.description: The highest-earning indie products by verified MRR (read from their payment provider, never self-reported): the Making Money board, top N (at most 50). Use for "which indie SaaS make the most" or "profitable micro-SaaS examples".

tools.name: get_stack_report
tools.description: Shipfolio's monthly State of the stack report: the most used tools overall and by category with their change against the previous month, fastest rising tools, common tool pairs, hosting platform share, cloud cost quartiles by provider and MRR band, tool use among products with verified MRR (median MRR band, never figures), pricing model mix and the month's launches. Anonymous aggregates: every figure counts at least five products, and no product is named. Cite the report's url. Without month, the latest published one.

month.description: The month, yyyy-MM (e.g. "2026-10"); leave out for the latest

tools.name: get_tool
tools.description: A developer tool or SaaS service in Shipfolio's catalog (Stripe, Supabase, Astro…) and who uses it ("which startups use Supabase"): what it is, pricing note, the features its website lists, how many products use it, the top 10 products built with it, tools it's often used with, and alternatives. For more products built with it, call search_products with tool.

slug.description: The tool's slug, e.g. "supabase" (search_tools finds it)

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Find tools in Shipfolio's catalog by name and category, most used first, each with how many products use it. At most 20 a page, 5 pages. Call get_tool for one tool, get_tool_pricing for its plans.

category.description: A catalog category, e.g. Database, Auth, Payments, Hosting or AI

tools.name: tool_alternatives
tools.description: Alternatives to a developer tool or service ("Vercel alternatives", "Firebase vs Supabase"): other tools in its category, most used first, and the tool and its top alternatives compared feature by feature, as each tool's own website describes it.

tools.name: get_tool_migrations
tools.description: Which tools public Shipfolio products replaced with this one (movingTo) and replaced it with (movingFrom), each with how many products made the move and its page, and the tool's adoption over the last twelve months (products using it at each month's end, products adding and removing it, net change). Only moves made by at least five products are listed, and any monthly figure under five is null: say "fewer than five" rather than guessing. Products are never named here; cite the urls.

slug.description: The tool's slug, e.g. "heroku" (search_tools finds it)

tools.name: get_tool_pricing
tools.description: A catalog tool's plans as Shipfolio last recorded them from its pricing page (name, monthly and yearly price in cents, unit for per-unit pricing, key limits, free tier, source and the date checked), and its published price changes, newest first, each with what changed. Plans are null until Shipfolio has approved a first reading. productCount is how many public products use the tool, shown only from five. Cite the url; prices can change after the date checked.

slug.description: The tool's slug, e.g. "vercel" (search_tools finds it)

tools.name: create_article_draft
tools.description: Drafts an article about one of the signed-in person's products: what they built, learned or launched. The body is Markdown (headings, lists, tables, links, code; no raw HTML). Calling twice makes two drafts. To show a product's tech stack, draft the text and then call add_stack_embed rather than typing a table of tools: the card stays current and links each tool. For search: the title is the page's search title, so keep it to 60 characters with the phrase people search for first; the subtitle is its search description, so make it one sentence of 120 to 160 characters saying what the reader gets; open with a paragraph that answers the title; give the body ## headings (they build the contents) and 300+ words; link to related Shipfolio pages. searchHints in the result says what this draft could still change. The article is saved as a draft only: nothing is published. The author reviews it, adds a cover image or data embeds and publishes it in the Shipfolio editor at editUrl. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

listing.description: The listing's slug or id the article is about

title.description: The headline and search title: 60 characters or fewer shows in full on Google, at most 120

body.description: The article in Markdown, at most 40,000 characters

subtitle.description: A one-sentence standfirst under the headline, used as the search description: 120 to 160 characters, at most 240

nicheTags.description: Up to 3 niche slugs from list_niches, e.g. ["invoicing"]

tools.name: update_article_draft
tools.description: Changes a draft article of the signed-in person's: only the fields given, the rest stay. Published articles can't be changed here. A new body replaces the whole body. For search: the title is the page's search title, so keep it to 60 characters with the phrase people search for first; the subtitle is its search description, so make it one sentence of 120 to 160 characters saying what the reader gets; open with a paragraph that answers the title; give the body ## headings (they build the contents) and 300+ words; link to related Shipfolio pages. searchHints in the result says what this draft could still change. The article is saved as a draft only: nothing is published. The author reviews it, adds a cover image or data embeds and publishes it in the Shipfolio editor at editUrl. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

articleId.description: The article's id, from create_article_draft or list_my_articles

title.description: A new headline and search title: 60 characters or fewer shows in full on Google, at most 120

body.description: The whole new body in Markdown, at most 40,000 characters

subtitle.description: A new one-sentence standfirst, used as the search description: 120 to 160 characters, at most 240

nicheTags.description: Replaces the niches: up to 3 slugs from list_niches

tools.name: list_my_articles
tools.description: The signed-in person's articles across their products, drafts and published, newest first, each with its editor link.

tools.name: list_embed_sources
tools.description: For one of the signed-in person's draft articles: the products it can chart (the article's own product first) and, per metric (MRR, cloud cost, cloud cost by provider, visitors, page views, website clicks, launch votes), whether there is data, where it comes from, the days it covers and, when missing, why. Call this before add_article_embed.

tools.name: add_article_embed
tools.description: Adds a live data embed (a line or bar chart, a period comparison, or headline stats) to one of the signed-in person's draft articles, from their own verified data, and places it in the body after the heading given (or at the end). Returns the figures it shows: quote those exactly in the text around it instead of guessing. Money values are in cents. A draft holds at most 6 embeds. Snapshot (the default) freezes the figures when the article is published; live keeps them current. The article is saved as a draft only: nothing is published. The author reviews it, adds a cover image or data embeds and publishes it in the Shipfolio editor at editUrl. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

product.description: The product to chart: a slug from list_embed_sources

kind.description: Line, Bars, Comparison (first period against the last) or Stat (one headline figure per metric)

range.description: The range: Last2Weeks, Last4Weeks, Last8Weeks, Last12Weeks, Last3Months, Last6Months, Last12Months, LaunchWeek or Custom

from.description: With Custom: the first day, yyyy-MM-dd

to.description: With Custom: the last day, yyyy-MM-dd

caption.description: A caption under the embed, at most 200 characters

afterHeading.description: Place it after the heading with this text, e.g. "What it costs to run"; at the end when left out or not found

live.description: true keeps the figures current after publishing; false (default) freezes them when published

tools.name: remove_article_embed
tools.description: Deletes a data embed from one of the signed-in person's draft articles and takes its line out of the body. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

tools.name: add_stack_embed
tools.description: Places a card of a product's tech stack (its tools grouped by category, each linking to the tool's Shipfolio page) in one of the signed-in person's draft articles, after the heading given (or at the end). Any product with a public Shipfolio page works, not only the person's own. Returns exactly the tools the card shows: write about those, not a stack you assume. Prefer this to typing a table of tools. The card is read live from public pages for every reader, so it stays current; if the product later stops being public, readers see a placeholder instead. A draft shows up to 12 cards. The article is saved as a draft only: nothing is published. The author reviews it, adds a cover image or data embeds and publishes it in the Shipfolio editor at editUrl. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

product.description: The product's slug, e.g. "trackwise" (search_products finds it)

afterHeading.description: Place it after the heading with this text, e.g. "What we built it with"; at the end when left out or not found

tools.name: add_product_embed
tools.description: Places a card of a product (logo, name, tagline, its verified MRR badge when it has one, and a link to its Shipfolio page) in one of the signed-in person's draft articles, after the heading given (or at the end). Any product with a public Shipfolio page works, not only the person's own. Returns what the card shows. The card is read live from public pages for every reader, so it stays current; if the product later stops being public, readers see a placeholder instead. A draft shows up to 12 cards. The article is saved as a draft only: nothing is published. The author reviews it, adds a cover image or data embeds and publishes it in the Shipfolio editor at editUrl. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

product.description: The product's slug, e.g. "trackwise" (search_products finds it)

afterHeading.description: Place it after the heading with this text; at the end when left out or not found

tools.name: add_tool_embed
tools.description: Places a card of a tool from Shipfolio's catalog (logo, name, category, a short description, how many products use it, and a link to its page) in one of the signed-in person's draft articles, after the heading given (or at the end). Returns what the card shows. The card is read live from public pages for every reader, so it stays current; if the product later stops being public, readers see a placeholder instead. A draft shows up to 12 cards. The article is saved as a draft only: nothing is published. The author reviews it, adds a cover image or data embeds and publishes it in the Shipfolio editor at editUrl. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

tool.description: The tool's slug, e.g. "supabase" (search_tools finds it)

afterHeading.description: Place it after the heading with this text; at the end when left out or not found

tools.name: post_ship_log_entry
tools.description: Posts "shipped X" to the public changelog of the signed-in person's product. Calling twice posts twice; followers can see it. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

shippedOn.description: The day it shipped, yyyy-MM-dd; today when left out

tools.name: schedule_launch
tools.description: Schedules the signed-in person's product on Shipfolio's launch board for a UTC day, or moves its scheduled launch there. The listing must be published with at least 3 tools in its stack, and the day can't be in the past. When get_my_listing shows a pending launchProposal, prefer answer_launch_proposal, which keeps or moves that booking. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

tools.name: answer_launch_proposal
tools.description: Answers the launch day Shipfolio booked for one of the signed-in person's products (launchProposal in get_my_listing, while Pending): keep confirms that day now, move launches on another day instead (today or later; openDays have room), cancel drops the booking for good and Shipfolio never books this product again, though the team can still schedule_launch. Keep and move put the product on the public launch board. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

day.description: With move: the launch day, yyyy-MM-dd (UTC)

tools.name: get_my_analytics
tools.description: Page views, visitors, website clicks, impressions, upvotes, new watchers and reviews for the last 7, 30 or 90 days against the period before: for one of the signed-in person's products (with top sources and referrers), or all of them.

listing.description: The listing's slug or id; all products when left out

tools.name: list_my_listings
tools.description: The signed-in person's own products (every product of a company they own or admin), drafts and private ones included: status, completeness and its next step (the empty field worth the most), stack size, verified MRR, launch, page views over the last 7 days against the 7 before (published products only), whether a Buffer is connected for social posts, and links to the public page and the editor. Start here: the other *_my_* tools take a slug or id from this list.

tools.name: get_my_listing
tools.description: One of the signed-in person's own products in full: every editable field, completeness gaps (what each empty field would rank for), stack, features (has, doesn't have, suggested from alternatives), FAQs with their ids, launch, the launch day Shipfolio booked for it if any (launchProposal; answer_launch_proposal keeps, moves or cancels a pending one), verified MRR, and margin: last full month's MRR against cloud cost, exact and private to the team, plus what the public page shows and what keeps it off. Sharing the cost publicly is the founder's own choice on the costs page; never suggest it is done for them.

listing.description: The listing's slug or id, from list_my_listings

tools.name: update_my_listing
tools.description: Changes fields of one of the signed-in person's own products: tagline, description (markdown), problem statement, niches, audience tags and the products it is an alternative to. Only the fields given change; a list replaces the old list. Overwrites what is there. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

problemStatement.description: The problem it solves, one or two sentences

niches.description: Niche slugs from list_niches; replaces the current ones. Unknown ones are refused with the closest valid slugs

audience.description: Audience tags; replaces the current ones

alternativeTo.description: Products it is an alternative to, by name; replaces the current ones

tools.name: add_my_feature
tools.description: Adds a feature the signed-in person's product has ("Two-factor authentication"). Shipfolio matches it to the shared feature list so comparisons line up. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

tools.name: set_my_feature
tools.description: Says whether the signed-in person's product has a feature already on its list or suggested from its alternatives: true, false, or null to take the answer back. Replaces the current answer. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

feature.description: The feature's slug or name, from get_my_listing

has.description: true: has it; false: doesn't; null: unanswered

tools.name: add_my_faq
tools.description: Adds a question and answer to the FAQ on the signed-in person's product page (20 at most). Calling twice adds it twice. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

tools.name: update_my_faq
tools.description: Rewrites one FAQ on the signed-in person's product, replacing its question and answer. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

tools.name: remove_my_faq
tools.description: Deletes one FAQ from the signed-in person's product page. It can't be undone. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

tools.name: set_article_cover
tools.description: Sets the cover image of one of the signed-in person's draft articles, replacing any cover it has. The image is cropped to 16:9 around its center at 1600 by 900, as the editor does. Published articles can't be changed here. Returns the cover's public address. Give the image exactly one way: uploadId, from create_image_upload once its file was sent (use it for any file on this machine or anything over about 50 KB, rather than base64); imageUrl, a public https address Shipfolio downloads (no private or local addresses); or imageBase64 with mimeType (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or image/gif), only for a tiny image. At most 8 MB (5 MB for a logo). It is re-encoded as WebP without its metadata. Counts as an image upload, which has its own daily limit; an uploadId was counted when its file arrived. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

articleId.description: The draft article's id, from create_article_draft or list_my_articles

uploadId.description: The uploadId from create_image_upload, after its file was sent to uploadUrl. Works once, within 15 minutes

imageUrl.description: A public https address of the image

imageBase64.description: A tiny image's bytes as base64 (a data: URL is accepted). For a file, use uploadId instead

mimeType.description: With imageBase64: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or image/gif

tools.name: list_my_screenshots
tools.description: The screenshot gallery of one of the signed-in person's own products, in the order it shows: each screenshot's id, public addresses, size, alt text, caption and device frame. Call this before remove_listing_screenshot.

listing.description: The listing's slug or id, from list_my_listings

tools.name: add_listing_screenshot
tools.description: Adds a screenshot at the end of one of the signed-in person's product galleries (at most 50 a product). It keeps its shape, scaled down so its longest side is at most 2000 pixels. Without alt text Shipfolio writes one from the image. Calling twice adds it twice. Returns its public addresses. Give the image exactly one way: uploadId, from create_image_upload once its file was sent (use it for any file on this machine or anything over about 50 KB, rather than base64); imageUrl, a public https address Shipfolio downloads (no private or local addresses); or imageBase64 with mimeType (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or image/gif), only for a tiny image. At most 8 MB (5 MB for a logo). It is re-encoded as WebP without its metadata. Counts as an image upload, which has its own daily limit; an uploadId was counted when its file arrived. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

uploadId.description: The uploadId from create_image_upload, after its file was sent to uploadUrl. Works once, within 15 minutes

imageUrl.description: A public https address of the image

imageBase64.description: A tiny image's bytes as base64 (a data: URL is accepted). For a file, use uploadId instead

mimeType.description: With imageBase64: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or image/gif

alt.description: What the screenshot shows, for screen readers and search, at most 160 characters

caption.description: A caption under it, at most 200 characters

device.description: The frame it is shown in: Desktop (a browser window, the default), Phone or Tablet

tools.name: remove_listing_screenshot
tools.description: Deletes one screenshot from one of the signed-in person's product galleries; the others keep their order. Returns the gallery as it is afterwards. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

screenshotId.description: The screenshot's id, from list_my_screenshots or add_listing_screenshot

tools.name: set_listing_logo
tools.description: Sets the logo of one of the signed-in person's own products, replacing the current one. The image is cropped to a square around its center at 256 by 256, as the editor does, so send a square logo. Returns its public address. Give the image exactly one way: uploadId, from create_image_upload once its file was sent (use it for any file on this machine or anything over about 50 KB, rather than base64); imageUrl, a public https address Shipfolio downloads (no private or local addresses); or imageBase64 with mimeType (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or image/gif), only for a tiny image. At most 8 MB (5 MB for a logo). It is re-encoded as WebP without its metadata. Counts as an image upload, which has its own daily limit; an uploadId was counted when its file arrived. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

uploadId.description: The uploadId from create_image_upload, after its file was sent to uploadUrl. Works once, within 15 minutes

imageUrl.description: A public https address of the image

imageBase64.description: A tiny image's bytes as base64 (a data: URL is accepted). For a file, use uploadId instead

mimeType.description: With imageBase64: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or image/gif

tools.name: create_image_upload
tools.description: Makes a single-use link to send an image file straight to Shipfolio, so it never has to be pasted into a tool call as base64. Use it for any image that is a file on this machine or larger than about 50 KB, in preference to imageBase64: call this, run the returned curl command with your shell, putting the image's path after the @ (or PUT the file's raw bytes to uploadUrl with any HTTP tool; POST works too), then pass uploadId to set_article_cover, add_listing_screenshot or set_listing_logo. The link needs no sign-in, takes one file of at most maxBytes, and expires after 15 minutes (expiresAt); the type is read from the file's bytes (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF). Making the link is free; the file counts as one image upload when it arrives, and the image tool doesn't count it again. Needs the write scope. It changes nothing by itself: confirm the change with the user before calling the image tool that uses it.

purpose.description: What the image is for: ArticleCover (set_article_cover), Screenshot (add_listing_screenshot) or Logo (set_listing_logo)

mimeType.description: The file's type, for the curl command's Content-Type: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or image/gif. Optional; Shipfolio reads the type from the bytes

tools.name: list_my_social_posts
tools.description: What one of the signed-in person's products posted to its own social accounts through its Buffer, newest first (the 20 newest): network, account, text, status (Queued, Published or Failed with the problem), what it was about, whether autopilot sent it, when, its link, and Buffer's impressions, engagements and clicks once read. Also which events autopilot posts by itself. Nothing is posted from here: the team writes, sends and switches autopilot in the product's Social section at socialUrl.

listing.description: The listing's slug or id, from list_my_listings

tools.name: add_to_my_stack
tools.description: Adds a catalog tool to the stack of the signed-in person's product, with an optional note and monthly cost. A launch needs at least 3 tools. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

category.description: Category; the tool's own when left out

note.description: What it's used for, at most 280 characters

monthlyCostUsd.description: Monthly cost in whole US dollars

tools.name: update_my_stack_item
tools.description: Changes the category, note or monthly cost of a tool already in the signed-in person's stack; fields left out stay. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

monthlyCostUsd.description: New monthly cost in whole US dollars

tools.name: remove_from_my_stack
tools.description: Removes a tool from the signed-in person's stack, with its note and cost. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

tools.name: list_my_updates
tools.description: The weekly build in public updates of the products the signed-in person manages, newest week first: drafts waiting, published and skipped ones, each with its editor link and, once published, its public page.

tools.name: draft_product_update
tools.description: Drafts the build in public update of one of the signed-in person's products for a week that has ended (last week by default), from that week's verified signals, or rewrites a waiting draft. Returns the week's facts with their exact figures: any title or body given must quote only those figures, exactly as written, or it is refused. Traffic and an unshared cloud cost come back as private notes and must not go in the text. Nothing is published: the founder reviews, shares and publishes it at editUrl. A published or skipped week can't be changed here. Needs the write scope. Before calling, show the user exactly what will change and wait for them to confirm.

week.description: The ISO week as yyyy-ww, e.g. "2026-46"; last week when left out

title.description: A title, at most 120 characters; written from the facts when left out

body.description: The update in Markdown, at most 4,000 characters; written from the facts when left out
